key_insight: Linking memory lessons to their source evidence helps LLM agents check unreliable guidance and avoid failures caused by memory.
engineering_relevance: Agent memory systems should preserve inspectable evidence, not just distilled lessons, so agents can verify guidance before acting.
method: Store each concise insight with links to a success/failure summary and its raw task trajectory.
Start new tasks with all insights, then inspect linked evidence using terminal tools when details are missing, lessons conflict, or a lesson comes from a failed task.
Use retrieved evidence to clarify or correct the lesson before acting.
evidence_signal: Across five agentic benchmarks, WikiTrace consistently outperformed existing memory approaches and a same-insights-only baseline while reducing memory-induced degradation.
watch_item: Retaining raw trajectories and inspecting evidence may add storage, context, and tool-use costs; the abstract does not quantify these overheads.
paper_title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
